endpoint: HSA binding affinity (Ka) and binary bind/no-bind, from its own differential scanning fluorimetry assay
model: 7 classifiers and 9 regressors (python/sklearn); best classifier logistic regression, best regressor support vector regression
trained_on: ITS OWN measurements: 65 PFAS from 20 chemical classes plus 3 fatty acids as non-fluorinated analogues; 57 chemicals reached the training set, one congener dropped for missing descriptors
descriptors: Saagar (834) + ToxPrints (729) + OPERA (12) = 1575 generated; invariant features removed and min-max scaled to 255 used
caveat: 255 features on 57 chemicals, about 4.5 per compound, and the only held-out data is the cross-validation fold. The DSF endpoint itself fails the physiological bound in binding_kd_physiological_bound.py (81 % bound at six sites, where plasma needs >99 %).

endpoint: HSA binding affinity (EC50, mM) and a high/low class at a 1.45 mM threshold
model: GA-LDA classification (DTC Lab ClassificationBasedQSAR v1.0.0); GA-MLR and PLS regression (SmallDataModeler v1.0); GenRA read-across on ToxPrint chemotypes; Glide XP docking on PDB 7AAI
trained_on: NOT ITS OWN. 24 PFAS EC50 values collected from the literature; the paper's description (24 PFAS, mM EC50 by 4-parameter variable slope, 4:2 and 6:2 FTOH non-binding, H/L threshold 1.45 mM) matches the Starnes 2024 cross-species DSF dataset
descriptors: alvaDesc 2.0.16: 753 2D descriptors offered for classification, 736 for regression. Classification retains 3 (average connectivity index of order 4, an augmented edge-adjacency eigenvalue, an eccentric topological index); regression retains 4 (packing density index, Moran autocorrelation lag 8 mass-weighted, Geary autocorrelation lag 8 vdW-volume-weighted, QED drug-likeness)
validation: classification split 2:1 at random, training n = 16 and test n = 8; regression used the whole set under exhaustive double cross-validation, no split. Docking validated by redocking PFOA, RMSD 0.092 A.
performance: ROC AUC 0.97 training, 1.00 on the 8-compound test set
applied_to: not applied to an external inventory
caveat: 753 descriptors searched against 16 training compounds, and a test AUC of 1.00 on eight. The retained descriptors are abstract topological indices with no stated mechanism. The authors say themselves that the GenRA predictions are 'not that reliable': every AUC was 0 and p ran 0.73 to 1.

endpoint: unbound fraction (f_unbound) in liver, brain, heart, kidney and lung
model: partial least squares regression, four separate models (human, C57, mouse, rat)
trained_on: ITS OWN measurements: 16 PFAS across four organisms, the 320 experimental rows this database holds
descriptors: 20 physicochemical properties from MOE 2018.01 and Dragon 6.0. Molecular weight and log D are the ones the paper reads a trend off.
validation: leave-one-out cross-validation over the 16 PFAS; grid search for the component count (4 for human, 3 for C57, mouse and rat). No external test set.
applied_to: not applied to an external inventory
caveat: 20 descriptors on 16 compounds. LOOCV on 16 is a weak test, but the descriptors are physicochemical rather than abstract and the training data are the paper's own, which makes this the cleanest of the binding models here.

endpoint: in vivo elimination half-life, as 4 bins (<12 h, <1 week, <2 months, >2 months)
model: random forest classifier
trained_on: NOT ITS OWN. In vivo half-lives curated by Lau et al. in four reviews (2007, 2012, 2015, 2021), across human, monkey, rat and mouse. The eleven PFAS are not enumerated in the sections read here.
descriptors: 22 physico-chemical (18 predicted by OPERA v2.7, a ToxPrint binary for a backbone ether bond, average molecular mass, 2 chain-length) + 88 transport/re-uptake analogue descriptors (structural similarity of defluorinated PFAS to endogenous chemicals, as a surrogate for transporter affinity) + physiological descriptors including kidney geometry, as a surrogate for transporter expression
validation: y-randomised null model as comparator; applicability domain by the method of Roy, Kar and Ambure. No external test set.
performance: 86.1 % accuracy against 32.2 % for the y-randomised null
applied_to: CCD PFAS master list: 6603 of 8163 had enough information, 4136 inside the domain across four species, 3890 for human
caveat: ELEVEN compounds in training, predicting 3890. The descriptor design is the most mechanistically motivated of any model here -- it builds explicit surrogates for renal transporter expression and affinity rather than searching a descriptor pool -- and the y-randomised comparator is the right control. The training set is still eleven compounds.

endpoint: apparent BSA binding constant as a function of ionic strength and salt identity
model: mechanistic competitive-salt binding model fitted to the paper's own fluorescence data
trained_on: ITS OWN measurements: Hill-equation Ka across a range of salt conditions
descriptors: n/a -- mechanistic parameters (Kas1, Kas2, KA1, KA2), not structural descriptors
validation: parameters fitted simultaneously across multiple salt conditions because a single condition does not give a unique fit; uncertainties from the covariance matrix
applied_to: prediction of Ka at unmeasured salt conditions
caveat: Not a QSAR -- no structure enters it. Listed because its fitted constants are model output, and because the paper states plainly that a single salt condition does not identify the parameters, which is the kind of admission most of the models here do not make.

model: molecular docking, AutoDock Vina, PDB 4E99
trained_on: nothing -- docking is not fitted to data
caveat: Rises monotonically with chain length (PFPrS -6.2, PFBS -6.4, PFHxS -7.5, PFOS -8.3), the same pattern as Li 2021's docking columns, where that paper's own measurements turn over above PFHpA. Two independent instances of structure-only scoring missing the turn. The paper's experimental constants are held out separately -- see audit_wu2024_hsa.py.

endpoint: HSA binding, geometric-mean log Ka from docking
model: molecular docking against PDB 1E7G and 1AO6
trained_on: nothing -- docking is not fitted to data
caveat: The two docking columns of SI sheet S7.2 are DELIBERATELY NOT INGESTED as values -- see add_li2021_hsa_si.py. They run up to 7.5 where the same sheet's measurements top out near 5.5, and they rise monotonically where the measurements turn over above PFHpA. That contrast is the reason the paper is worth having.

model: AutoDock4 binding energies, reported alongside the paper's own thermal-shift (QITSA) measurements
trained_on: nothing -- docking is not fitted to data
caveat: Separate from the docking: Han's QUOTED hL-FABP constants are held out of the L-FABP figure, because its own notes say they were taken from other papers rather than measured. Its own measurements are thermal-shift dTm, not a dissociation constant.

model: molecular docking (Glide, Schrodinger Maestro) plus a machine-learning QSAR built on the docking scores
trained_on: NOT ESTABLISHED -- full text not reachable. The method string says the ML is built ON THE DOCKING SCORES, which would make it a model of a model rather than of any measurement, but that is not confirmed against the paper
caveat: No PMC record and the publisher gates the page, so neither full text nor abstract was reachable. NOTE there are TWO Zhao 2023 papers in this database and they are easy to confuse: this one, in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety, carries the L-FABP docking and the ML QSAR; 10.1016/j.envint.2023.107951 in Environment International is a review with no primary data. Needs institutional access.

endpoint: narrative review of PFAS binding across serum albumin, liver FABP and organic anion transporters
model: literature review; no primary measurements and no fitted model
trained_on: the published literature, not re-analysed
caveat: A review, listed so it is not mistaken for the other Zhao 2023 above, and so its single database row is not read as a measurement.

endpoint: predicted HSA binding and binding rate in blood
model: molecular modelling
trained_on: nothing fitted
caveat: Held only as a SECONDARY transcription from OEHHA 2024 PFOA/PFOS PHG Table A6.2; the primary paper has not been retrieved and no assay or modelling conditions are available. Its predicted f_unbound values (0.05, 0.02) are predictions, not measurements.

model: one-variable linear regression: log D_lip/w = 0.535 N + 0.658 on the number of fluorinated carbons (eq S10)
trained_on: ITS OWN measured log D_lip/w values
descriptors: the number of fluorinated carbons -- one physical variable, not a descriptor pool
caveat: Only the 2 PREDICTED rows are computed; Qin's other 94 rows in this database are measurements and are not affected. One mechanistically plain variable and a stated R2 -- the opposite end of the spectrum from a 753-descriptor search, and worth holding up as such.

model: mechanistic protein-binding bioconcentration model coupling albumin in the circulatory and extracellular space, FABP in liver, and OAT-facilitated renal elimination and reabsorption
trained_on: parameterised from published in vitro binding data
caveat: A process model, not a QSAR: no structural descriptor enters it. Its parameters come from the same in vitro binding literature this database holds, so it is not independent of those measurements.

endpoint: comparison of two competing mechanisms for tissue distribution
model: review and comparison of phospholipid partitioning against protein interaction as competing models
trained_on: the published literature
caveat: Concludes protein interactions are needed to explain tissue distribution, the chain-length relationship and species- and sex-specific half-lives, and that the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive.

model: PBPK model adaptation plus a systematic literature review of which binding parameters are available at all
trained_on: published binding parameters
caveat: The review half is the useful half here: it documents which protein-binding parameters are and are not available for PBPK, which is the same gap this project keeps running into.

model: physiologically based toxicokinetic model parameterised from in vitro binding, permeability and transporter data
trained_on: published in vitro binding, permeability and transporter data
performance: sensitivity analysis: permeability and phospholipid binding dominate elimination and distribution of long-chain PFAA (nPFC >= 7), while elimination of short-chain PFAA (nPFC <= 6) is more sensitive to other terms
caveat: Full text on disk at literature/fulltext/Fischer 2025.txt; the sensitivity result above is from the abstract and sensitivity analysis, and the model's parameter provenance has not been read in detail.

model: COSMO-RS prediction alongside dialysis (K_mem/w) and planar lipid bilayer permeability (P_ion) measurements
trained_on: nothing -- COSMO-RS is first-principles
caveat: The measurements are experimental and are kept; only the COSMO-RS strand is computed. A first-principles prediction with no training set is a different kind of claim from a 753-descriptor fit, and is tagged separately for that reason.

model: molecular docking alongside a fluorescence competitive binding assay and TH-responsive cell proliferation
trained_on: nothing fitted
caveat: Experimental rows are kept; the docking component is the computed strand.

model: in silico homology modelling alongside an in vitro competitive binding assay with recombinant LBD protein
trained_on: nothing fitted
caveat: A modelled protein STRUCTURE rather than a predicted affinity. Experimental rows are kept.

model: molecular docking and molecular dynamics alongside spectroscopy and retinol-binding kinetics
trained_on: nothing fitted
caveat: Experimental rows are kept; docking and MD are the computed strand. Beta-lactoglobulin is a milk protein, not a plasma transport protein.
